text: After a difficult day, which response from your partner would stay with you the longest?

options.label: A
options.text: They tell me they are proud of how I handled it.

options.label: B
options.text: They put everything aside and spend the evening with me.

options.label: C
options.text: They quietly take something off my plate.

options.label: D
options.text: They bring me something small they remembered I like.

options.label: E
options.text: They hold me close without needing to talk.

text: Your partner has had an exhausting week. What do you instinctively want to do first?

options.label: A
options.text: Tell them exactly what you appreciate about them.

options.label: B
options.text: Make uninterrupted time for them.

options.label: C
options.text: Handle one of their responsibilities for them.

options.label: D
options.text: Surprise them with something meaningful.

options.label: E
options.text: Sit close, hug them, or touch their hand.

text: Imagine your partner says, 'I know you love me, but sometimes I don't feel it.' Which response would most likely repair the moment?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Let me tell you what you mean to me.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'Let's spend some time together�just us.'

options.label: C
options.text: 'Tell me what I can take care of for you.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'I saw this and immediately thought of you.'

options.label: E
options.text: You move closer and embrace them.

text: Which absence would be hardest for you to explain away in a relationship?

options.label: A
options.text: Rarely hearing affection or appreciation.

options.label: B
options.text: Rarely having real time together.

options.label: C
options.text: Feeling that everything is left for me to handle.

options.label: D
options.text: Never receiving thoughtful gestures.

options.label: E
options.text: A lack of affectionate touch.

text: Your partner remembers something tiny you mentioned months ago. What makes the moment meaningful?

options.label: A
options.text: They remembered because they listened to me.

options.label: B
options.text: They turned it into a thoughtful surprise.

options.label: C
options.text: They use it to do something helpful for me.

options.label: D
options.text: They mention it affectionately and tell me why they remembered.

options.label: E
options.text: They pull me close while mentioning it.

text: When you picture a perfect ordinary evening together, what matters most?

options.label: A
options.text: Talking openly about the day.

options.label: B
options.text: Doing something together without distractions.

options.label: C
options.text: Cooking, organizing, or preparing something together.

options.label: D
options.text: Having a small surprise waiting for one another.

options.label: E
options.text: Sitting close, cuddling, or touching naturally.

text: Your partner is upset but says, 'I'm fine.' What are you most likely to do?

options.label: A
options.text: Ask gently and tell them they can say anything to me.

options.label: B
options.text: Stay with them and let them decide whether to talk.

options.label: C
options.text: Start helping with whatever seems to be overwhelming them.

options.label: D
options.text: Bring them something comforting.

options.label: E
options.text: Reach for their hand or hug them.

text: If your partner had to choose one sentence, which would feel most revealing about how they want to be loved?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Tell me what you appreciate about me.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'Make time for me when life gets busy.'

options.label: C
options.text: 'Notice what needs doing and help without me asking.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Remember the little things that matter to me.'

options.label: E
options.text: 'Come closer when I need you.'

text: During an argument, what would help you feel that the relationship is still safe?

options.label: A
options.text: Hearing reassurance that we still care about each other.

options.label: B
options.text: Knowing we will have uninterrupted time to resolve it.

options.label: C
options.text: Seeing the other person take responsibility through action.

options.label: D
options.text: A meaningful gesture after the conflict.

options.label: E
options.text: A hug or affectionate contact once we are calm.

text: Which kind of disappointment would make you feel most invisible?

options.label: A
options.text: They rarely acknowledge what I do.

options.label: B
options.text: They are physically present but mentally somewhere else.

options.label: C
options.text: They see that I am overwhelmed but do nothing.

options.label: D
options.text: They forget meaningful occasions or details.

options.label: E
options.text: They become physically distant when I need closeness.

text: Your partner achieves something they worked hard for. What feels most natural?

options.label: A
options.text: Tell them specifically how proud I am.

options.label: B
options.text: Make the occasion about spending time together.

options.label: C
options.text: Help make their next step easier.

options.label: D
options.text: Give them something connected to the achievement.

options.label: E
options.text: Hug them and celebrate physically.

text: If you were away from your partner for several weeks, what would you miss most?

options.label: A
options.text: Their messages and words.

options.label: B
options.text: The experience of simply being together.

options.label: C
options.text: Having someone who naturally helps with everyday things.

options.label: D
options.text: The little things they would normally bring or leave for me.

options.label: E
options.text: Their physical presence and touch.

text: Your partner asks, 'How do you know I love you?' What answer comes most naturally?

options.label: A
options.text: 'Because of the way you speak to me.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'Because you make time for me.'

options.label: C
options.text: 'Because you show up when I need you.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Because you notice things about me.'

options.label: E
options.text: 'Because I feel it when you hold me.'

text: What kind of romantic surprise would stay in your memory longest?

options.label: A
options.text: A letter explaining what I mean to them.

options.label: B
options.text: A whole day planned around us.

options.label: C
options.text: They arrange something that removes a burden I have been carrying.

options.label: D
options.text: Something personal they chose because it reminded them of me.

options.label: E
options.text: A private, affectionate moment together.

text: When you feel disconnected from your partner, what do you reach for first?

options.label: A
options.text: A real conversation.

options.label: B
options.text: Time alone together.

options.label: C
options.text: Doing something helpful for them.

options.label: D
options.text: A thoughtful gesture.

options.label: E
options.text: Physical closeness.

text: Which sentence would hurt most if your partner said it sincerely?

options.label: A
options.text: 'I don't really notice what you do.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'I don't need to spend time with you to feel close.'

options.label: C
options.text: 'You don't need to help me; I'll handle everything alone.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'Those little things don't mean anything to me.'

options.label: E
options.text: 'I don't really like being touched.'

text: Imagine your partner has had a terrible day but does not want advice. What would you give instead?

options.label: A
options.text: Reassuring words.

options.label: B
options.text: Your full attention without trying to fix it.

options.label: C
options.text: Practical relief from whatever still needs to be done.

options.label: D
options.text: Something comforting you know they like.

options.label: E
options.text: A hug or quiet physical closeness.

text: Which pattern would make you wonder whether your partner still feels emotionally connected to you?

options.label: A
options.text: Their affectionate language disappears.

options.label: B
options.text: They stop making intentional time for us.

options.label: C
options.text: They stop helping or showing practical consideration.

options.label: D
options.text: They stop remembering the little things.

options.label: E
options.text: They stop reaching for me physically.

text: When you apologize, which part feels most important to you?

options.label: A
options.text: Saying clearly what I am sorry for.

options.label: B
options.text: Giving them time and attention to talk it through.

options.label: C
options.text: Changing something practical afterward.

options.label: D
options.text: Doing something thoughtful afterward.

options.label: E
options.text: Reconnecting physically once things are calm.

text: If your partner could change one small habit tomorrow, which would make the biggest emotional difference?

options.label: A
options.text: Express appreciation more often.

options.label: B
options.text: Put the phone away and be fully present.

options.label: C
options.text: Notice what needs to be done without being asked.

options.label: D
options.text: Remember small occasions and preferences.

options.label: E
options.text: Initiate affection more naturally.

text: What do you secretly wish your partner understood without you having to ask?

options.label: A
options.text: How much their words affect me.

options.label: B
options.text: How much their attention matters.

options.label: C
options.text: How meaningful it is when they make life easier.

options.label: D
options.text: How much small details stay with me.

options.label: E
options.text: How much closeness calms me.

text: Your partner says they feel loved by you, but you are not sure they actually do. What do you examine first?

options.label: A
options.text: Whether I tell them enough.

options.label: B
options.text: Whether I give them enough real time.

options.label: C
options.text: Whether my actions match what I say.

options.label: D
options.text: Whether I remember what matters to them.

options.label: E
options.text: Whether I show affection physically.

text: Which moment feels most intimate without necessarily being romantic?

options.label: A
options.text: Someone saying something vulnerable and honest.

options.label: B
options.text: Sitting together in comfortable silence.

options.label: C
options.text: Doing an ordinary task for each other.

options.label: D
options.text: Finding an unexpected little reminder of each other.

options.label: E
options.text: Resting against each other without speaking.

text: Your partner is busy for a long period. Which change would you notice first?

options.label: A
options.text: Fewer affectionate messages.

options.label: B
options.text: Fewer moments of undistracted time.

options.label: C
options.text: Less practical consideration.

options.label: D
options.text: Fewer thoughtful gestures.

options.label: E
options.text: Less physical affection.

text: If you could preserve one thing from your relationship during a difficult period, what would you protect?

options.label: A
options.text: The way we speak kindly to each other.

options.label: B
options.text: Our private time together.

options.label: C
options.text: The way we help each other.

options.label: D
options.text: Our little traditions and gestures.

options.label: E
options.text: Our physical closeness.

text: What would make you feel most chosen by your partner?

options.label: A
options.text: They tell me why they choose me.

options.label: B
options.text: They consistently make space for me.

options.label: C
options.text: They show up when life is difficult.

options.label: D
options.text: They notice and remember what matters to me.

options.label: E
options.text: They naturally seek closeness with me.

text: Your partner gives you a gift that is inexpensive but deeply personal. What matters most?

options.label: A
options.text: The message they included.

options.label: B
options.text: That they took time to find something personal.

options.label: C
options.text: That they solved a small problem for me through the gift.

options.label: D
options.text: That they remembered something specific about me.

options.label: E
options.text: That they gave it to me with affection and closeness.

text: When your relationship feels strong, which sentence best describes the feeling?

options.label: A
options.text: 'I feel understood.'

options.label: B
options.text: 'I feel like we really share a life.'

options.label: C
options.text: 'I know we can rely on each other.'

options.label: D
options.text: 'I feel remembered even when we are apart.'

options.label: E
options.text: 'I feel at home when we are close.'

text: What is the clearest sign that your partner has truly listened to you?

options.label: A
options.text: They respond to what I actually said.

options.label: B
options.text: They remember it later and make time to return to it.

options.label: C
options.text: They change something they do because of it.

options.label: D
options.text: They remember a detail I thought they would forget.

options.label: E
options.text: They respond with affectionate closeness.

text: If you had to describe the deepest thing you want from a long-term relationship, which feels closest?

options.label: A
options.text: To feel emotionally valued and spoken to with love.

options.label: B
options.text: To feel that we continually choose time for each other.

options.label: C
options.text: To know we will carry life's burdens together.

options.label: D
options.text: To feel that even after years, we still notice the little things about each other.

options.label: E
options.text: To feel physically and emotionally at home with each other.
